newsitem.title: UK: LME copper creeps down in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper creeps down in late trading.

text.p: LME copper held at lower levels after losing grip on the $1,900 per tonne area after the kerb close.
Shortly after the end of the kerb, where the last trade was at $1,900, prices broke through support and quickly dipped to a low indication of $1,875/80.
But by 1800 GMT, the market had recovered to be quoted at $1,888/92.
Dealers and analysts said the market had been weakened by another failure on the upside this week, bigger contangos and widespread speculative sales.
Most of the other metals were little changed, except nickel, which edged down to $7,330/60 from a kerb close of $7,380.
Tin was a touch softer at $6,080/100 from $6,100/05.
